scenario.name: Microsoft Sysinternals & Splunk SURGe DFIR — LSASS MiniDump via comsvcs.dll & Sysmon EventID 10
scenario.overview: Picture a clean city hospital ward with a red-cross triage check-in desk, curtained patient exam bays, a wall of labeled medicine cabinets, and rolling stainless-steel medical carts. Walking briskly past the hospital triage desk in a borrowed white lab coat, an intruder grabs a spare clipboard and wheels a rolling medical cart down the ward corridor. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the patient chart & medicine cart, then smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches. The head triage nurse checks the electronic shift roster at the nurse station and spots a lab-coat visitor who was never assigned to that hospital ward. On a Windows workstation (MITRE T1003.001), an attacker enables debug privileges, then uses the signed comsvcs.dll MiniDump export through rundll32 to snapshot lsass.exe memory into an on-disk MDMP file without loading a known credential-theft tool. Steps #1 cover privilege adjustment and process discovery in Security logs, Step #2 analyze cross-process OpenProcess and MiniDump calls in Sysmon EventID 10, and Step #3 verify the minidump header and offline credential parsing from file-create telemetry. Primary detection pivots on Sysmon process access to lsass.exe with broad GrantedAccess masks and a CallTrace that includes comsvcs.dll or MiniDumpWriteDump.

stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1134 - Access Token Manipulation: SeDebugPrivilege)

stages.title: Stage 2: Cross-Process OpenProcess & MiniDumpWriteDump via comsvcs.dll (Sysmon EventID 10)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.001 - OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory)
stages.description: Because every nurse assumes someone pushing an official medical cart belongs on shift, the intruder pulls confidential patient charts and opens the medicine supply drawer. Here in Step 2 inside the hospital ward, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the triage nurse's station without disturbing the sealed clean-supply closet. The attacker executes rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll,MiniDump 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin full. Internally, comsvcs.dll invokes OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS 0x1FFFFF) on lsass.exe and calls dbghelp.dll!MiniDumpWriteDump, which Sysmon EventID 10 captures with CallTrace entries pointing directly through comsvcs.dll and dbgcore.dll (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with EventID=10 , Sysmon ProcessAccess / 4656 , Security Object Handle, SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe, TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF , PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS, CallTrace=ntdll.dll -> KERNELBASE.dll -> comsvcs.dll -> dbgcore.dll so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll,MiniDump 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin full (which invokes the signed Windows proxy binary rundll32.exe to load C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll and call its MiniDump export , or ordinal #24, passing so that dumps the full virtual memory of lsass.exe to disk , T1003.001 using a built-in Microsoft DLL , comsvcs.dll -> MiniDumpWriteDump instead of dropping third-party tools like procdump.exe or mimikatz.exe, triggering Sysmon EventID 10 with GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF). Next, the follow-up artifact rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll,#24 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin full # Ordinal #24 bypasses naive CLI filters runs (which invokes the signed Windows proxy binary rundll32.exe to load C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll and call its MiniDump export , or ordinal #24, passing so that dumps the full virtual memory of lsass.exe to disk , T1003.001 using a built-in Microsoft DLL , comsvcs.dll -> MiniDumpWriteDump instead of dropping third-party tools like procdump.exe or mimikatz.exe, triggering Sysmon EventID 10 with GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll,MiniDump 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin full / ⇠#2 ACK 10) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Win32 Process Manager (CSR)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 lsass.exe (PID 684 Memory)).

stages.title: Stage 3: MDMP Magic Header (4D 44 4D 50) File Creation & Offline Pypykatz Parsing (Sysmon EventID 11)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.001 - Minidump File Artifact & Offline Parsing)
stages.description: Quietly photocopying records onto a hidden notepad while standing beside the exam bay, the intruder wheels the cart right back toward the elevator lobby. In this final step inside the hospital ward, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches until the nurse station chart audit catches the mismatch. dbgcore.dll writes the complete LSASS virtual memory snapshot to C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin beginning with the 4-byte Windows Minidump signature 4D 44 4D 50 ("MDMP"). Sysmon EventID 11 logs the creation of the dump file by rundll32.exe before the attacker exfiltrates it to parse wdigest, msv1_0, and kerberos structures with pypykatz (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with EventID=11 , Sysmon FileCreate, Image=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe, TargetFilename=C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin, FileHeaderSignature=4D 44 4D 50 , MDMP Minidump so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 11: Image=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe TargetFilename=C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin (which executes Microsoft's signed rundll32.exe host binary to load a target DLL into memory and directly invoke its exported function entrypoint , Sysmon so that proxies execution of malicious DLL code , T1003.001 through a trusted, Microsoft-signed system binary during "MDMP Magic Header , 4D 44 4D 50 File Creation & Offline Pypykatz Parsing , Sysmon EventID 11" to evade application allowlisting and process-name heuristics). Next, the follow-up artifact File Header Magic: 4D 44 4D 50 93 A7 00 00 ("MDMP" Minidump Header) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , File Header Magic: 4D 44 4D 50 93 A7 00 00 , "MDMP" Minidump Header via System / Runtime Exe so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "MDMP Magic Header , 4D 44 4D 50 File Creation & Offline Pypykatz Parsing , Sysmon EventID 11" , dbgcore while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll,MiniDump 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin full / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Win32 Process Manager (CSR)) to Node ④ (#4 rundll32.exe (comsvcs.dll)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 lsass.exe (PID 684 Memory)).

steps.storyAnalogy: Quietly photocopying records onto a hidden notepad while standing beside the exam bay, the intruder wheels the cart right back toward the elevator lobby. In this final step inside the hospital ward, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches until the nurse station chart audit catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: dbgcore.dll writes the complete LSASS virtual memory snapshot to C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin beginning with the 4-byte Windows Minidump signature 4D 44 4D 50 ("MDMP"). Sysmon EventID 11 logs the creation of the dump file by rundll32.exe before the attacker exfiltrates it to parse wdigest, msv1_0, and kerberos structures with pypykatz (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with EventID=11 , Sysmon FileCreate, Image=C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe, TargetFilename=C:\Windows\Temp\debug.bin, FileHeaderSignature=4D 44 4D 50 , MDMP Minidump so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

Next, the follow-up artifact File Header Magic: 4D 44 4D 50 93 A7 00 00 ("MDMP" Minidump Header) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , File Header Magic: 4D 44 4D 50 93 A7 00 00 , "MDMP" Minidump Header via System / Runtime Exe so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "MDMP Magic Header , 4D 44 4D 50 File Creation & Offline Pypykatz Parsing , Sysmon EventID 11" , dbgcore while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
